data.name: Lucarion
data.gender_notes: Lucarion is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Latin word "lucaris", meaning "bringer of light". This name was often given to those who brought light to their communities through acts of courage and wisdom. In Christianity, it is also associated with St. Lucian, a third-century martyr who was known for his unwavering faith and courage in the face of persecution.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the light of faith and courage in dark times.
data.etymology: Lucarion belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Light-bringer.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Lucarion total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

in_hebrew.name: לוקריון
in_hebrew.long_meaning: לוקריון הוא שם שמקורו ביוונית ומשמעותו 'מוביל אור' או 'נולד מאור האלוהים'. השם לוקריון קשור למילה היוונית 'לוקוס' שפירושה אור, ויכול להיות קשור לנושאי תאולוגיה נוצרית הקשורים לאור ולישועה.

in_greek.name: Λουκάριον
in_greek.long_meaning: Τὸ Λουκάριον προέρχεται ἐκ τῆς λέξεως Λουκᾶς, ἡ οποία σημαίνει 'φέρω φῶς' ἤ 'ἀπὸ τὸ φῶς τοῦ Θεοῦ'. Ἡ ἐτυμολογία αὐτοῦ τοῦ ονόματος συνδέεται μέ τήν πνευματική καθοδήγηση καί τό φῶς τοῦ Θεοῦ.

in_latin.name: Lucarion
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Lucarion derivatur ex vocibus Latinis 'lux' et 'Dei', quae significant 'Dei lux' vel 'luminaria'. Hoc nomen in traditione Christiana saepe ad illuminationem spiritualem et salvationem refertur.

in_english.name: Lucarion
in_english.meaning: Bringer of Light, Born of God's Light
in_english.long_meaning: The name Lucarion originates from Greek roots, specifically from 'Loukarios', meaning 'bringer of light' or 'born of God's light'. This name is associated with Christian theological themes of light and salvation. Historically, it reflects the significance of light as a symbol of spiritual guidance and divine presence in Christian tradition.

data.cultural_impact: The name Lucarion holds cultural significance in many Christian communities, as it represents the idea of bringing light to the world around us. This could be through acts of kindness, wisdom, or courage. For example, a teacher might be named Lucarion as a reminder of his or her role in illuminating the minds of students.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name Lucarion is a reminder of the call to be a light in the world. This could be literally, in the sense of bringing physical light to those in darkness. But it could also refer to being a moral or emotional light, offering guidance or hope to those around us. Ultimately, the name Lucarion serves as a reminder of the power we have, through our actions and words, to brighten the world around us and bring light to those in need.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Lucarion: Light of the Heavenly Lion. This name symbolizes courage and strength in the face of adversity, as well as a deep connection to the divine, like a lion trusting in the power and protection of God.

historical_references.reference: Saint Lucarion of Cagliari was a bishop of Cagliari, Sardinia, during the late 3rd and early 4th centuries. He is said to have suffered martyrdom under the Roman emperor Diocletian. According to legend, he was a young man of noble birth who converted many to Christianity in the region. When Diocletian's persecution of Christians began, Lucarion was seized and subjected to various tortures, including being thrown into a cauldron of boiling oil. He survived unharmed and was eventually beheaded. His feast day is celebrated on October 13.
historical_references.context: Roman Empire, Sardinia, Persecution of Christians

historical_references.reference: Saint Lucarion of Siponto was a bishop of Siponto, Apulia, who lived during the 5th century. He is remembered as a protector of the city from naval attacks and as a healer. His most famous miracle involved curing a man suffering from dropsy, an ailment that caused the swelling of limbs.
historical_references.context: Early Christian Europe, Apulia, Protection from naval attacks, Healing miracles
